pagedattention.d: vLLM technique (Kwon et al., SOSP 2023) that stores the KV cache in fixed-size blocks scattered across memory, located through a per-request block table, like an operating system's virtual memory. It does away with contiguous reservation and with almost all fragmentation.

fragmentacao-interna.d: Space wasted inside an allocation: the end of a fixed-size reservation that its owner doesn't use. In PagedAttention it is limited to the last block of each request, at most block_size − 1 tokens per group.

fragmentacao-externa.d: Free memory chopped into holes between live allocations, none of them big enough for a contiguous request. It disappears when every allocation has the same size (blocks), because any free block works for any request.

block-table.d: The list, per request and per KV group, of the physical block IDs in logical order. The attention kernel walks it to read the KV. It has a fixed width (block_table_stride) and is stored row after row; empty positions point to the null block.

block-pool.d: The vLLM structure that owns every physical KV block: global IDs shared by all groups, the free-block queue and, with prefix caching, the hash → block table. ID 0 is the null block.

null-block.d: ID 0 of the BlockPool, reserved as a marker and never filled. Empty table entries and blocks that have left a sliding window point to it; that's why a pool of 643 IDs has 642 usable ones.

bloco-de-kernel.d: The KV manager allocates in blocks of block_size tokens; the attention kernel was compiled for a page of its own (64 tokens in GLM's sparse-MLA kernels on SM12x). The worker splits each manager block into virtual kernel blocks, which cannot be done with padded pages.

mmc.d: The smallest integer divisible by all the given numbers. In hybrid vLLM, the scheduler block is the LCM of the groups' block sizes (3,584 in GLM, 256 in DeepSeek): prefix hits and state checkpoints align to it.

kv-cache-spec.d: The vLLM V1 description of how a layer type stores KV: FullAttentionSpec, MLAAttentionSpec, SlidingWindowSpec, MambaSpec… It defines the page, the block size and the maximum memory per request; layers with the same spec form a KV group.

alocador-kv-hibrido.d: The part of vLLM that manages models with several layer types: one manager per KV group, a coordinator and a single BlockPool with global IDs and pages of the same size in bytes. In it, IDs (not bytes) are usually the scarce resource.

pagina-uniforme.d: Rule of the hybrid allocator: every KV group uses pages of the same size in bytes, so any ID can serve any group. If the recurrent state is larger than the attention page, vLLM increases the attention block size (GLM: 3,584 tokens) and pads the state.

slot-share.d: GLM's mode for the KV of the DFlash2 drafter: a window group with 64-token blocks and a padded page equal to the MLA page; drafter layer i co-owns MLA tensor i on disjoint IDs. It adds no bytes to the pool, but charges one ID per block.

paginas-compactas-drafter.d: GLM53_DRAFT_KV_COMPACT=1: the drafter block becomes the largest multiple of 64 that divides the MLA block and fits in the page (896 at TP2, 640 at TP3). It cuts the admission IDs from 65 to 6 per request; it is not a measured VRAM reduction.

workspace-manager.d: The manager of vLLM's shared scratch buffers. Kernels request buffers (get_simultaneous) during the boot's dummy pass; after lock_workspace() nothing new can be allocated, which protects CUDA graph capture. Everything it holds comes out of the KV budget.

concorrencia-maxima.d: A vLLM boot line: the pool's IDs divided by the sum, over the groups, of the IDs a request of max_model_len takes. Multiplied by max_model_len, it becomes the “GPU KV cache size” line, which in hybrid models is not the size of the cache.

pool-kv-fixo.d: --kv-cache-memory-bytes N (or --kv-cache-memory): pins the KV pool per GPU in bytes, bypassing the profile run value. gpu_memory_utilization no longer applies to the KV, and host headroom becomes the responsibility of whoever configures it.

extent-kv.d: In TensorFold, the contiguous range [base, base + size) of rows of the per-token cache pool that belongs to a live stream or holds earlier conversations' kept prompts (several, when they are prefixes of one another). Base and size are multiples of 2,048 tokens; the kernels read a view of it as a tensor of their own, with no block table. It grows in place, moves or gets compacted when room runs out.

slot-por-fluxo.d: In TensorFold, each concurrent stream's fixed memory, outside the per-token pool: KDA recurrent state in two parities, convolution windows and the verify window's scratch. There is one slot per stream (PARALLEL, up to 4), allocated at startup.

compactacao-extents.d: Undoing external fragmentation by sliding every range of the pool down to the lowest free rows, so the free space becomes a single range. In TensorFold it is a series of MOVE operations that copy only the used rows, decided by rank 0 and applied identically by rank 1.
